   Lions’ man for big moments Shawal Anuar eyeing ‘dream come true’ run-out against Brazil

 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise Shawal Anuar sees Singapore’s match against five-time world champions Brazil as a “dream come true” after starting as an amateur who earned $50 per game and did odd jobs.
 He rose late to professional football, signed his first contract at 23, and has since won major trophies with Hougang United and Lion City Sailors, plus 20 goals in 61 Lion appearances.

 SINGAPORE – From once juggling odd jobs while earning $50 a game as an amateur footballer, Lions striker Shawal Anuar is now preparing for a challenge only a select few get: playing against five-time world champions Brazil.
 It was only 12 years ago that the wiry forward worked as a mover, cleaned glass panels at malls, and delivered kick scooters while he played for Keppel Monaco in the lower-tier National Football League (NFL).
 Unlike many of his peers, Shawal did not sign his first professional contract until he was 23 and so Singapore’s international friendly against Brazil at the National Stadium on Nov 17 is a proposition the striker’s younger self would have dismissed as inconceivable.
 “If I get to play against Brazil, I think it will be a really special experience,” the 35-year-old told The Straits Times ahead of the game, which is part of the Mizuho Blue Challenge – The Kallang Football Series Singapore.
 “Back then (when I was in NFL), I would have told you it was impossible for me to play against a team like Brazil and to be where I am now. But I think with the hard work I’ve put in from back then until now, and the opportunities I’ve been given throughout my journey, it shows that anything is possible with hard work and determination.
 “To play against a team like Brazil is a dream come true.”
 Shawal inked his first professional contract in 2014 after he was spotted by current Geylang International head coach Noor Ali, who was then the Eagles’ Prime League (reserve league) assistant coach.
 He made his international debut for Singapore two years later, then moved to Hougang United where he lifted the Singapore Cup, before signing for Singapore Premier League (SPL) powerhouses Lion City Sailors in 2023.
 With the Sailors, he has won two Singapore Premier League titles and the Singapore Cup another three times.
 This rags-to-riches-like tale is not lost on the humble Shawal, who said that as a youngster he fell in love with Brazil’s “skills, their style of play... everything”, and idolised iconic players such as Ronaldinho and, more recently, Neymar.
 Despite his late entrance to the highest level of the game, Shawal has made the most of his time at the top, and has proven himself a man for the big moments.
 In July 2023, he scored for the Sailors in a friendly match against English Premier League Tottenham Hotspur, and in December 2024, drilled home a sumptuous long-range effort against regional kingpins Thailand – both at the National Stadium.
 Last November, he scored a crucial equaliser as Singapore beat Hong Kong 2-1 in a historic Asian Cup qualifier at Kai Tak Stadium to secure the Lions’ first qualification for the continental tournament.
 Shawal, who has scored 20 goals in 61 appearances for the Lions and can play anywhere across the front three, said a goal against Brazil would be the most special of them all.
 More importantly, he hopes his journey – from where he started representing club and country and scoring important goals along the way – can empower budding footballers.
 He said: “I hope I can inspire all generations, especially kids, to chase their dreams like playing against all these big teams or representing your country.
 Shawal Anuar scoring the crucial equaliser against Hong Kong during the 2-1 win in November 2025.
 PHOTO: FOOTBALL ASSOCIATION OF SINGAPORE
 “My story has shown that if you keep believing and working hard, and never give up, you can keep pushing yourself until you get where you want to be.”
 The nippy striker, who is still one of the quickest in the team despite being in his 30s, has had to adjust to being an impact player for country as well as at his club, where he competes with several foreign imports for a place in the starting XI.
 This season, he has started just once in the SPL – where he has two goals in four matches – and made two appearances off the bench in the continental Asian Champions League Two.
 Noting that the “transition” has happened over some time, Shawal said: “I think I’ve gotten used to it. I’ve always told any coach I’ve played for that I’ll be ready whenever they call upon me. Whether it’s the last five minutes or the last 10 minutes, I’ll go in and give my best.”
 Singapore head coach Gavin Lee, in the pre-game press conference at the National Stadium on Nov 16, told the media that his players were ready to “compete” for longer than they did in the 4-1 defeat by Paraguay on Nov 13.
 The Lions had earned the praise of Paraguay coach Gustavo Alfaro, who noted that they “struggled to keep up with the pace” only “towards the end” of the game, when the South Americans threw on stars such as EPL players Diego Gomez and Julio Enciso, and former Newcastle United midfielder Miguel Almiron.
 Asked if he would employ an ultra defensive approach by “parking the bus”, Lee responded: “To be honest, it’s the same as how we prepared for Paraguay. I don’t think we planned to park the bus in that sense.
 “But there will be moments in the game where playing quality opposition like that forces you back naturally. In those moments where we need to park the bus, we just have to do it well.
 “However, as much as possible, one thing we always try to do is defend as far away from our goal as possible, because it’s the most logical thing to do. So tomorrow will be no different. But (then) again, it’ll be against Brazil.”
 World No. 6 Brazil’s friendly against 148th-ranked Singapore at the National Stadium on Nov 17 marks the final day of the Mizuho Blue Challenge – The Kallang Football Series Singapore. The quadrangular series kicked off with Paraguay’s 4-1 win over the Lions on Nov 13 before Japan beat Brazil 3-2 a day later.
 After the Singapore-Brazil clash on Nov 17, world No. 33 Paraguay will take on 17th-ranked Japan.
